thread:
alex: Heads up — opened PR that does a modules/ reorg (moves our in-repo modules to modules/registry layout), pulls provider blocks out of child modules, and updates top-level provider constraints to require aws >= 4.0. CI is failing because .terraform.lock.hcl doesn't match. Can someone quick-check the plan + whether we should relax constraints for the migration window?

maya: On it. PR is https://git.internal/r/infra/merge_requests/789 :eyes:

ricardo: I looked at the CI logs — error is 'provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws: version 3.73.0 found, but constraint is >= 4.0'. Seems some modules still pin a 3.x provider in their required_providers or have implicit 3.x usage.

alex: Right — we have a couple of forked modules that default to 3.x. I updated our forks to allow >=3.50, <5 but left root at >=4.0 to nudge upgrades. If that's too aggressive we can relax root to >=3.50 for a week while we finish refactors.

tanya: I'd prefer keeping root >=4.0 to avoid drift, but agree we need a canary path. Suggest: keep root at >=4.0, merge to a staging workspace first. If plan shows issues, roll back. Also note: v4 -> v3 resource diffs for some ecs/eks resources may need manual state rename. Add migration steps to PR.

ricardo: For the CI error specifically, easiest fix is to regenerate the provider lockfile from a clean init and commit the updated .terraform.lock.hcl. Run something like:

```
terraform init -upgrade
terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64
git add .terraform.lock.hcl && git commit -m "regen: provider lockfile"
```

alex: I added that to the PR description and will push a lockfile commit. Also included a snippet for state moves we'll need for EKS IAM roles.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline #1123: plan failed on merge request 789 — terraform validate failed (lockfile mismatch)

maya: When you push the lockfile, I'll run a staging plan and smoke test the EKS changes. One more thing: our modules/auth used to name a k8s secret as "auth-creds" but with the reorg the module path changed and the default name switched to "auth-credentials". We need to ensure SealedSecrets/ExternalSecrets wiring in prod won't break — include a migration in the PR notes.

alex: Good catch. Added migration entry and a tiny kubectl snippet folks can run to rename secrets if needed:

```
kubectl get secret -n prod auth-creds -o yaml | sed 's/name: auth-creds/name: auth-credentials/' | kubectl apply -f -
```

tanya: LGTM for the lockfile regen approach. @alex ping me after you push and CI shows a plan for staging; I'll approve and we can merge the canary into staging first :rocket:

alex: Pushed the regen + migration notes, CI started: https://ci.internal/pipelines/1124 :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: CI pipeline #1124: plan for staging succeeded

ricardo: Also a reminder — update any Makefile/terragrunt wrapper that calls terraform init with the old module paths. CI caught a couple of those in integration jobs.

alex: Thanks — I'll follow up with a tiny Makefile fix PR after this merges. Appreciate the quick checks, team :heart:
